sourceTitle: The Stock Market Is Being Used as a Dumping Ground
title: Companies Now Go Public To Cash Out, Not Raise Money
hook: Companies now list to cash out, not to raise money.
question: Who is buying the exit?

sources.name: Information asymmetry (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: one party has more or better information than the other

sources.name: Lock-up period (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: a predetermined amount of time following an initial public offering

sources.name: Greater fool theory (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: resold at an even higher price

scenes.narration: An IPO is supposed to raise money so a company can build and grow. More and more, though, it is really an exit, with insiders cashing out.
Think about what that means. When a company goes public, you are on the opposite side of the smartest sellers in the entire room.
The seller almost always has more and better information than the buyer.
Insiders are even locked up for ninety to a hundred eighty days after listing, and then they are free to sell.
That lock-up window is written directly into the deal.
And it shows in the results. Most of twenty twenty-one's new listings later fell below their IPO price.
It can rhyme with the greater fool theory, where someone always hopes to resell higher.
So when insiders are rushing for the exit, who exactly is buying it?
